gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many pixels each screen adds per video output or per pound. Two figures show it: the 16-inch stacked Duex Float 2 Pro adds 4,096,000 pixels through one video connection at 2.9 lb. The dual-14-inch FOPO S1 needs two video connections to add a similar 4,147,200 pixels at 3.13 lb, and on a laptop that drives only one external display it adds 2,073,600.
standout_why: I opened itechguides.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' (cited) and rottenwifi.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' (cited) on 2026-11-18. Both list scattered weights (Duex Float 2 Pro 2.9 lb, Vixtan triple 3.0 lb, KYY 1.7 lb) and resolutions. Neither works out pixels per pound, pixels per video connection, weight per added screen, or what a two-screen extender shows on a laptop that drives one external display. Neither gives a weight for any FOPO model. deskfinds.com returned 403, so I couldn't compare against it.
decides: The finding backs the stacked 16-inch Float 2 Pro as the pick for a laptop that drives only one external display or has one video-capable USB-C port: it gives about twice the added pixels of any 1080p extender through that one output and weighs less than the FOPO S1. Mobile Pixels' own fit range for it is 15–16-inch laptops, so smaller laptops can't use it. On a laptop with two video-capable USB-C ports, the FOPO S1 matches its pixel count with two side screens. The S1 wins the 'two extra screens' segment, but each screen needs its own video connection.
